findings.claim: The plan touches two concepts and the decisions index but never says whether supersede appends a log.md line. The every-touched-concept-is-logged rule (.claude/rules/okf-bundle.md) is a gate in this repo, and the okf plugin logs every supersession as a lifecycle event. A supersede that leaves log.md alone gives the caller a change the okf check refuses. Either way works, but the scope must say which: kmctl appends a dated bullet naming both ids, or kmctl leaves that to the caller and says so in its output. Done-when should cover it.

Invariant I4 (.okf/manifesto.md) says kmctl uses only fields the OKF v0.2 spec defines (stale_after, verified, sources, status) and adds no extension fields. The plan's core output is decision_status, which is not a spec field (okf_validate.py knows only status). The repo's own records and okf-bundle.md use decision_status, so the conflict is in the contract, not the code: the test written for I4 would catch this command. The operator needs to say decision_status is a bundle convention kmctl may write, by rewording I4 or accepting the risk in the plan, before it is built.
The plan now appends a dated log.md line naming both concept ids, and done-when covers the log, which meets every-touched-concept-is-logged.
The plan now writes only status (a spec field the okf validator accepts as deprecated) and never touches decision_status, so I4 holds as worded.

The index marker is appended to the line that holds the link, so on a wrapped index entry it lands in the middle of the description. This repository's own decisions index wraps every entry, so the first real use corrupts it.
test_supersede_links_both_ways checks only for "## Correction, " and never checks that a date follows, so an undated section passes r2's fails_when.

test_supersede_refusals checks only for a nonzero exit, so an uncaught exception (exit 1 with a traceback) passes as a refusal. It should assert the one-line "refused:" message on stderr, and it does not cover the same-id or missing-index-entry refusals.
_number uses str.isdigit, which accepts Unicode digits such as "²"; int() then raises ValueError and the CLI prints a traceback instead of a refusal.

The cli-interface rule is not fully met. The decision group's help does not name its prerequisites (a bundle from kmctl init, records from kmctl new decision). The already-deprecated and self-supersede refusals name no next command. The missing-index-entry refusal points to kmctl check, which reports the problem but does not fix it.

entries.change: The superseded note goes after the last line of a wrapped index entry, a decision number must be ASCII digits, and the self, already-deprecated and missing-entry refusals each name their fix.
The decision group's help names its prerequisites, kmctl init and kmctl new decision.
Tests for a wrapped entry and a missing index entry; r2 checks the Correction heading carries a date; r5 checks exit 1 and a refused line on stderr, including self-supersede and a non-ASCII digit.

findings.claim: the superseded note landed mid-entry on a wrapped index entry
the r2 test did not check that the Correction heading is dated
the r5 test did not check refused on stderr or cover the same-id and missing-entry cases
a non-ASCII digit crashed with a ValueError traceback
group help lacked prerequisites and refusals lacked a next step
